actions.name: drive forward at 30 % without a distance

control_flow: driveInTheDark: if the right light is more than 75 %, drive forward at 30 %; else call stopAtWall.
stopAtWall: if an obstacle is ahead, stop; else call followLine.
followLine: if the line tracker sees black, curve left; else curve right.

likely_intent.description: Drive through the tunnel and come out on the other side.

decision_points.condition: the right light sensor reads more than 75 %

branches.outcome: the light is bright: it drives forward at 30 %
the light is not bright: it calls stopAtWall
an obstacle is ahead: it stops
no obstacle is ahead: it calls followLine
it sees black: it curves left
it does not see black: it curves right

input_dimensions.dimension: what is ahead in the dim light
where the line tracker is relative to the line
what is ahead in the dim light

scenarios.coded_response: In bright light it drives forward at 30 %; in the dim tunnel, with no obstacle ahead, it follows the line: curve left on black, curve right otherwise.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot starts in bright light before a tunnel, with a black line running through the tunnel and nothing in the way.
scenarios.trigger: It drives into the tunnel: the right light drops below 75 % and the line tracker alternates between black and not black.
scenarios.title: Gets through the tunnel
assumptions: A black line runs through the tunnel for the robot to follow.
The tunnel has nothing in the robot's way and is wide enough.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It follows the line through the tunnel and comes out on the other side.

scenarios.coded_response: It stops and stays stopped while the obstacle is ahead.
scenarios.initial_condition: The robot is inside a tunnel in dim light, and a wall or obstacle is ahead across its way.
scenarios.trigger: The front obstacle sensor sees the wall or obstacle.
scenarios.title: Stops at a wall in the tunnel
assumptions: You didn't say what it should do at a wall in the tunnel; stopping is what the program is built to do.
scenarios.expected_response_hypothesis: It stops before the wall or obstacle without bumping into it.

uncertainties: You didn't say there is a line in the tunnel, but the program needs one to follow in the dark.
Inside a tunnel the right light sensor reads below 75 %, so the program goes on to stopAtWall there.
The program loops without waiting, so each movement block replaces the last one almost at once.
The line follower curves right whenever the line tracker is not on black, so without a line it would turn into a tunnel wall.
